units.text: EXT. LAKESIDE BOATHOUSE - DUSK
A weathered boathouse leaning over green water.
Paper lanterns hang from the rafters, half of them unlit.
A phonograph on an upturned crate turns a record, scratchy and slow.
THEODORA "TEDDY" LUND, 30s, in a yellow dress that has seen better summers, sits on the dock with her feet in the water.
Next to her, ARMAND BELLWETHER, 30s, a rower's shoulders under a rumpled linen shirt, holds two glasses and a bottle without a label.
Behind them on the boathouse porch stand her sister CORINNE, 40s, arms folded, and Armand's father OLD MR. BELLWETHER, 70s, in a cardigan, who has said nothing since they arrived.
Armand, you're going to drop it.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: I'm not going to drop it.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: You're holding it like a baby.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: A baby wouldn't have a cork.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: Teddy. Dinner.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: In a minute, Cor.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: You said that an hour ago.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: I meant it then too.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Armand pours.
The wine is pale.
They clink.
Old Mr. Bellwether coughs once and turns toward the water.
Father, you want some?
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: I want to know why my son is sitting on a dock in a good shirt.
units.name: OLD MR. BELLWETHER

units.text: Because I've been meaning to ask her something.
units.name: ARMAND

units.text: Then ask.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: He sets his glass down.
A dragonfly lands on its rim.
Corinne's arms unfold.
